tasks.title: Resolve the 32-bit Int money columns vs the contract's line-item maxima (blocked on a frozen-artifact decision)
tasks.acceptance: After the user/architect decides which frozen artifact moves: EITHER (a) data-model + prisma/schema.prisma widen Invoice.totalCents and InvoiceLineItem.amountCents to BigInt with an additive migration, the service/DTO boundary keeps returning JSON numbers within Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER, and a vitest case proves a contract-maximum line item (quantity 1000 x unitPriceCents 100000000) round-trips exactly; OR (b) api-contract.yaml tightens LineItemInput.quantity/unitPriceCents (and adds an invoice-total bound) so no contract-legal input can produce a value above 2147483647, with an authored VALIDATION_FAILED message per REQ-009 and a vitest case asserting the rejection. Either way `npm test`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, `npm run build` and `npx playwright test` exit 0, and the frozen-artifact SHA-256 values in .oma/state.json are updated to match.
tasks.notes: Answers oma-backend's Q-004, and corrects its premise. There is NO ~$21.5M cap on the shipped stack: SQLite INTEGER is 64-bit and the Prisma driver adapter passes the value straight through. QA created a real invoice at contract-legal maxima (quantity 1000 x unitPriceCents 100000000) — POST returned 201 with totalCents 100000000000, GET /invoices and GET /dashboard both read it back exactly, and the raw sqlite column holds 100000000000 as typeof 'integer'. No v1 symptom exists. The defect is portability: Prisma Int on PostgreSQL is a 4-byte INTEGER (max 2147483647), and ADR-001 — the entire justification for the sqlite override — promises a v2 Postgres move is a driver-adapter + migration swap. Rows this API accepts today cannot follow that migration. So api-contract.yaml (maxima at :805-814) and data-model.md (Int columns) are mutually inconsistent under a guarantee ADR-001 makes; both are frozen, so neither remedy is available to a dev agent without a change request. BLOCKED pending that decision — do not start implementation. Escalated as contract_changes in handoff seq 19. Not a v1 malfunction; do not treat this as urgent ahead of T-025.

tasks.title: Raw Zod default text still reaches `details` on container type mismatches (object/array), including a missing `lineItems`
tasks.acceptance: Every one of these probes returns 400 VALIDATION_FAILED whose `details` values contain none of the substrings 'Invalid input', 'expected object', 'expected array', 'Too big', 'Too small': (1) POST /api/clients with body `"hello"`, `5`, `null`, `[]`; (2) POST /api/auth/signup with body `[]`; (3) POST /api/invoices/{id}/status with body `"paid"`; (4) PATCH /api/clients/{id} with body `1`; (5) POST /api/invoices with `lineItems` set to `"nope"`, `5`, `{}`; (6) POST /api/invoices with `lineItems` OMITTED entirely. Add a vitest case per class in src/shared/schemas/schemas.test.ts so reverting the message turns `npm test` red. `npm test`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, `npm run build`, `npm run format:check` and `npx playwright test` all still exit 0.
tasks.notes: T-025 is genuinely done for FIELD-level constraints: QA fuzzed all 11 boundary/input schemas over 130 distinct (field,message) pairs and every field-level message is authored prose, including the four run-2 named and the three extra oma-backend added. But oma-backend's handoff seq 21 claim -- 'no raw Zod default text reaches `details` from any input schema any more' -- is false as stated. Two constructs still emit Zod defaults: (a) the top-level `z.object(...)` on EVERY input schema, when the JSON body parses but is not an object -> details._ = 'Invalid input: expected object, received string'; (b) `z.array(lineItemInputSchema)`'s invalid_type, when `lineItems` is a non-array OR is missing -> details.lineItems = 'Invalid input: expected array, received undefined'. Verified over HTTP against `next start` on :3551, 11 distinct probes, run-3. Reachability: NOT reachable from the app's own forms (they always send a well-shaped object), so this is API-surface only -- the same severity class as F-3 was in run 1, not the user-reachable class F-5 was. The missing-`lineItems` case is the most plausible: a normal API-client mistake. Fix shape: `z.object({...}, { error: 'Provide the request body as a JSON object.' })` on each input schema, and `z.array(lineItemInputSchema, { error: 'Add at least one line item.' })`.

tasks.title: Dashboard fails entirely for contract-legal invoice totals above Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER (centsSchema is stricter than the frozen contract)
tasks.acceptance: Create one invoice with 100 line items at the contract maxima (quantity 1000000, unitPriceCents 100000000 -> totalCents 10000000000000000), then load /dashboard in a browser: the Outstanding figure renders and the recent-invoices list renders; the error banner 'Couldn't load your dashboard.' does NOT appear. Add a vitest case pinning that `centsSchema` (and `dashboardSchema`/`invoiceSummarySchema` through it) accepts a value above Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER, so reverting the fix turns `npm test` red. `npm test`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, `npm run build`, `npm run format:check` and `npx playwright test` all still exit 0.
tasks.notes: src/shared/schemas/common.ts:29 `centsSchema = z.number().int().min(0)`. In Zod 4, `.int()` is a SAFE-integer check: it rejects anything above 9007199254740991 with 'Too big: expected int to be <=9007199254740991' (verified directly against the installed zod 4.4.3). The frozen api-contract declares `totalCents: { type: integer, minimum: 0 }` with NO maximum, so the schema is stricter than the contract it is supposed to mirror. Consequence, reproduced live on the production build: ONE contract-legal POST /api/invoices (100 line items at the maxima) yields totalCents 10000000000000000; the API stores and returns it exactly, /invoices and /invoices/{id} both render it correctly ($100,000,000,000,000.00), but /dashboard's client-side `totalsSchema.safeParse` fails and the screen shows only 'Couldn't load your dashboard.' -- the whole screen, not a degraded figure. Same break for the dashboard AGGREGATE, which is a sum over all unpaid invoices and has no contract bound at all. NOT a regression from T-026/ADR-006: SQLite already stored 64-bit values in v1, so this predates the widening. Related to but distinct from Q-005: Q-005 is about JSON-number precision on the wire and needs an api-contract change; this one is a code-side schema that contradicts the contract as frozen and can be fixed without touching any frozen artifact. Probable owner oma-backend because src/shared/schemas/ is backend-written per stack.md's directory contract, though the symptom surfaces in oma-frontend's dashboard screen -- disagree in your handoff if the error-state policy in screens/dashboard.md is the real subject.
